headline: AUKING MINING LOCKS UP 75% OF GREENLAND NIOBIUM/RARE EARTH PROJECT — BINDING TERM SHEET FOR QEQERTAASAQ ADDS CRITICAL MINERALS FOOTPRINT
snippet: AuKing Mining (ASX: AKN) signed a binding term sheet on October 13 to acquire up to a 75% interest in the Qeqertaasaq niobium and rare earth project in western Greenland. The deal adds a Greenland-jurisdiction critical minerals asset to AuKing's portfolio at a time when Western-government competition for Greenland rare earth and niobium projects is intensifying — the US-Denmark-Greenland security framework signed in September 2026 has sharpened the race for Greenland critical mineral acreage. Further details on project grades, capital structure and development timeline are expected as due diligence advances toward definitive agreements.

headline: NSW DISCOVERY: EVERGREEN HITS 13m AT 3.3g/t GOLD AND 264g/t SILVER — AUSTRALIAN GOLD AND COPPER AWAITS 16 MORE RC HOLES
snippet: Australian Gold and Copper (ASX: AGC) reported October 13 that initial reverse circulation assays from the Evergreen Discovery in New South Wales returned 13m at 3.3 g/t gold and 264 g/t silver — a high-silver result that flags polymetallic potential alongside the gold system. Sixteen of 21 holes drilled remain unreported, with results expected through October and early November; the company is targeting a maiden JORC resource once the full assay program is complete.

headline: URANIUM WEEK: PALADIN, DEEP YELLOW AND PENINSULA ALL DOWN AS ASX NAMES BLEED — LONG-TERM CONTRACT PRICES HOLD 18-YEAR HIGH AT $96.50/lb
snippet: FNArena's October 13 Uranium Week review reports that Australian uranium equities suffered another difficult week — Paladin Energy, Deep Yellow (which hit a 52-week low), Peninsula Energy and Boss Energy all fell, with the broader sector down 3-8% on risk-off selling and Middle East energy-security concerns — even as long-term contract prices remained at an 18-year high near $96.50 per pound and spot held at $90. The equity-versus-commodity disconnect widened further. Paladin Energy is scheduled to release September-quarter production results on October 14.

headline: COPPER BULLS GET GEOPOLITICAL LAYER: IRAN OIL TANKER HIT IN STRAIT OF HORMUZ AS CHILE'S TRIPLE LABOUR CRISIS STILL UNRESOLVED
snippet: LME copper held near $14,621 per tonne on October 13 as an overnight attack on an Iranian oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz added a geopolitical risk premium on top of Chile's existing supply crisis — Escondida supervisors are on strike and Centinela remains paralysed by a hunger-striking union. Shanghai Metals Market's morning meeting noted that post-holiday Chinese restocking sentiment has softened, capping further upside. COMEX copper held near $6.70 per pound, close to August's all-time record of $6.80, leaving the market balanced between a weakening short-term demand signal out of China and three compounding supply-side risk vectors.

headline: CENTRAL BANKS BOUGHT 289 TONNES IN Q2 2026 — SO WHY ARE GOLD MINERS FALLING 2-5X HARDER THAN SPOT GOLD THIS OCTOBER?
snippet: Discovery Alert's October 2026 analysis investigates the growing paradox at the heart of the gold sector: official institutions purchased a net 289 tonnes in Q2 2026, central bank buying is tracking toward a fourth consecutive record year, and ETF holdings reached an all-time high of 4,256 tonnes — yet gold mining equities have shed 2 to 5 times more than spot gold during the September–October correction, with Sibanye Stillwater and Harmony Gold at one point falling as much as 7.92% in a single premarket session. The analysis points to cost inflation, company-specific execution risk and retail investor preference for physical gold and ETFs over producer equity as the primary culprits. For self-directed investors evaluating the sector discount, the piece offers a framework: compare producer free cash flow margins at current gold prices, not price-recovery assumptions.

headline: FT: GOLD MINER M&A IS "FINALLY PRODUCING SOMETHING THAT GLITTERS" — WHY 2026'S WAVE OF DEALS IS NOTHING LIKE THE 2010S DISASTERS
snippet: A Financial Times analysis republished on GoldSeek argues that 2026's wave of gold sector consolidation — including the Equinox-Orla combination, Discovery's Porcupine acquisition and the A$12.6 billion Genesis-Vault merger — marks a qualitative shift from the value-destroying M&A of the 2010s. The difference: deals are structured at disciplined NAV multiples with acquirers buying near-development assets and operating mines, not greenfield exploration plays. Cash-rich senior producers now have the technical teams and balance sheet strength to capture real synergies, making the current cycle accretive to shareholders. For junior mining investors, the FT's framing implies that near-development assets held by quality juniors now carry a credible takeout premium rather than the speculative M&A hope of a decade ago.

headline: ANGLO-TECK COPPER MEGA-MERGER EXPECTS CHINA APPROVAL BY YEAR-END — SAMR STANDS AS FINAL REGULATORY HURDLE IN $53B DEAL
snippet: Anglo American has guided investors to expect a decision from China's State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) on the Anglo-Teck copper merger by year-end, according to Industrial Info Resources. SAMR is the last outstanding regulator — South Korea cleared the deal in April 2026 — and has reportedly sought assurances that the combined entity will maintain steady copper concentrate flows into China. The all-share merger, valued at approximately US$53 billion, would create one of the world's top copper producers. A year-end approval window matters to the junior copper space: deal completion could trigger further consolidation as the combined entity begins portfolio optimisation and potential asset sales.

headline: WGC 2026 CENTRAL BANK SURVEY: 71% OF RESPONDENTS EXPECT GOLD'S SHARE OF GLOBAL RESERVES TO KEEP RISING — STRUCTURAL FLOOR CONFIRMED
snippet: The World Gold Council's 2026 Central Bank Gold Reserves Survey, highlighted on GoldSeek, finds that 71% of responding central banks expect gold's share of global reserves to increase over the next twelve months — a new survey record. Emerging market institutions led in planned buying intentions, citing geopolitical risk diversification and the erosion of dollar reserve value as primary motivations; 94% cited gold's role as a safe haven. The survey provides the structural context behind 2026's record ETF inflows and persistent central bank accumulation: even as spot prices correct from January's $5,589 peak, the institutional demand floor for gold continues to widen, supporting the long-term investment thesis for junior mining investors.
